chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was listening, and he said: 'Sometimes we command a man to buy for us land, a house, a slave, and a female slave, and we give him a fee/commission.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.جُعْلًا: A fee or commission paid to an agent for a specific service
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a commission fee to a broker for purchasing property or slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical application of *ju'lah* (commission-based agency) in early Shia jurisprudence, specifically validating remuneration for agents purchasing diverse assets like real estate and slaves. It underscores the flexibility of Shia commercial law in accommodating service-based compensation, a principle that remains foundational for modern brokerage and agency contracts.
